label: Acts 1:1
text: The first book I wrote, Theophilus, concerned all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,

label: Acts 1:2
text: until the day in which he was received up, after he had given commandment through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen.

label: Acts 1:3
text: To these he also showed himself alive after he suffered, by many proofs, appearing to them over a period of forty days, and speaking about God’s Kingdom.

label: Acts 1:4
text: Being assembled together with them, he commanded them, “Don’t depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which you heard from me.

label: Acts 1:5
text: For John indeed baptized in water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit not many days from now.”

variants.reading: ἐν πνεύματι βαπτισθήσεσθε ἁγίῳ ('with [the] Spirit will be baptised Holy')
variants.note: Sinaiticus* and B, with 81, 915 and Didymus (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles, Acts 1:5).

label: Acts 1:6
text: Therefore when they had come together, they asked him, “Lord, are you now restoring the kingdom to Israel?”

label: Acts 1:7
text: He said to them, “It isn’t for you to know times or seasons which the Father has set within his own authority.

label: Acts 1:8
text: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”

label: Acts 1:9
text: When he had said these things, as they were looking, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.

label: Acts 1:10
text: While they were looking steadfastly into the sky as he went, behold, two men stood by them in white clothing,

label: Acts 1:11
text: who also said, “You men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into the sky? This Jesus, who was received up from you into the sky, will come back in the same way as you saw him going into the sky.”

label: Acts 1:12
text: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day’s journey away.

label: Acts 1:13
text: When they had come in, they went up into the upper room, where they were staying; that is Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas the son of James.

label: Acts 1:14
text: All these with one accord continued steadfastly in prayer and supplication, along with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.

label: Acts 1:15
text: In these days, Peter stood up in the middle of the disciples (and the number of names was about one hundred twenty), and said,

variants.note: Sinaiticus, A, B, C*, 33 vid and others; the reading is 'of the brothers' (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles, Acts 1:15).

label: Acts 1:16
text: “Brothers, it was necessary that this Scripture should be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke before by the mouth of David concerning Judas, who was guide to those who took Jesus.

label: Acts 1:17
text: For he was counted with us, and received his portion in this ministry.

label: Acts 1:18
text: Now this man obtained a field with the reward for his wickedness, and falling headlong, his body burst open, and all his intestines gushed out.

variants.note: Sinaiticus, A, B, C, D, E, Psi, 049 and the vast majority (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles, Acts 1:18).

label: Acts 1:19
text: It became known to everyone who lived in Jerusalem that in their language that field was called ‘Akeldama,’ that is, ‘The field of blood.’

label: Acts 1:20
text: For it is written in the book of Psalms, ‘Let his habitation be made desolate. Let no one dwell therein;’ and, ‘Let another take his office.’

label: Acts 1:21
text: “Of the men therefore who have accompanied us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,

label: Acts 1:22
text: beginning from the baptism of John, to the day that he was received up from us, of these one must become a witness with us of his resurrection.”

label: Acts 1:23
text: They put forward two, Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also called Justus, and Matthias.

label: Acts 1:24
text: They prayed, and said, “You, Lord, who know the hearts of all men, show which one of these two you have chosen

label: Acts 1:25
text: to take part in this ministry and apostleship from which Judas fell away, that he might go to his own place.”

label: Acts 1:26
text: They drew lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.

label: Jesus was taken up into the sky and a cloud received him (the ascension)
statement: Jesus was taken up while the apostles watched, and a cloud received him out of their sight (1:2 'received up', 1:9).

label: Jesus showed himself alive to the apostles over forty days
statement: After his suffering Jesus showed himself alive to the apostles by many proofs, appearing to them over a period of forty days.

label: Olivet is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day's journey away
statement: The mount called Olivet, from which the apostles returned to Jerusalem, is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day's journey away.

label: A Sabbath day's journey was the permitted Sabbath walking limit, 2,000 cubits
statement: A Sabbath day's journey was the distance a Jew was permitted to walk on the Sabbath, fixed at 2,000 cubits (about 920-1,200 m).

label: The apostles lodged in an upper room in Jerusalem
statement: After the ascension the apostles went up into an upper room in Jerusalem where they were staying.

label: The number of the disciples gathered was about one hundred twenty
statement: In the days after the ascension the number of names gathered together in Jerusalem was about one hundred twenty.

label: Judas was guide to those who took Jesus and was counted with the Twelve
statement: Judas, who was guide to those who took Jesus, was counted with the apostles and received his portion in their ministry.

label: Judas bought a field, fell headlong and burst open; the field was called Akeldama
statement: Judas obtained a field with the reward of his wickedness, fell headlong, and his body burst open; the field was called Akeldama, 'the field of blood', in Jerusalem's own language, and it became known to everyone living in Jerusalem.

label: Peter quoted Psalm 69:25 and Psalm 109:8 about Judas
statement: Peter quoted from the book of Psalms: 'Let his habitation be made desolate, let no one dwell therein' (Psalm 69:25) and 'Let another take his office' (Psalm 109:8).

label: Matthias was chosen by lot to replace Judas
statement: The disciples put forward Joseph Barsabbas and Matthias, prayed, cast lots, and the lot fell on Matthias, who was counted with the eleven apostles.

label: Cenacle (the traditional Upper Room), Mount Zion
periods: Gothic structure of the 12th-14th centuries CE; Christian tradition locating the Last Supper here is older

label: Wikipedia: Cenacle (the Upper Room)
title: Cenacle
excerpt: is a room in Mount Zion in Jerusalem , just outside the Old City walls , traditionally held to be the site of the Last Supper , the final meal that, in the Gospel accounts, Jesus held with the apostles

label: Great-circle distance Mount of Olives to the Temple Mount
method: Great-circle (haversine) distance computed from the graph's Wikipedia coordinates: Mount of Olives (31.7794 N, 35.2454 E) to the Temple Mount (31.7779 N, 35.2354 E) = 960 m. Two thousand cubits at 46-60 cm per cubit = 920-1,200 m, so the Mount of Olives lies within one Sabbath day's journey of the Temple.

label: Wikipedia: Sabbath day's journey (the 2,000-cubit techum)
title: Sabbath day's journey
excerpt: Originally, the 2,000 cubit Sabbath limit was measured with a standard 50-cubit rope.

label: Wikipedia: Akeldama (the two accounts of Judas's death)
title: Akeldama
excerpt: There are two accounts of his death. The Gospel of Matthew describes how Judas returned the money to the Temple authorities before hanging himself.

label: Sefaria: Mishnah Eruvin 5:7 (the 2,000-cubit limit)
title: Mishnah Eruvin 5:7
excerpt: One who was in a large city and placed his eiruv in a small city, or one who was in a small city and placed his eiruv in a large city, may walk through the entire city in which he placed his eiruv and another two thousand cubits beyond it

label: Sefaria: Mishnah Eruvin 4:3 (outside the Shabbat limit)
title: Mishnah Eruvin 4:3
excerpt: regard to one whom gentiles forcibly took him out beyond the Shabbat limit, or if an evil spirit took him out, i.e., he was temporarily insane, and found himself outside the Shabbat limit, he has only four cubits that he may walk from where he is standing.

label: Sefaria: Mishnah Tamid 3:7 (four daily Temple lotteries)
title: Mishnah Tamid 3:7
excerpt: Four lotteries were conducted in the Temple each day in order to determine which priests would perform which of the Temple rites.

label: Psalm 69:25 (WEB, bible-api)
title: Psalm 69:25 (World English Bible)
excerpt: Let their habitation be desolate. Let no one dwell in their tents.

label: Psalm 109:8 (WEB, bible-api)
title: Psalm 109:8 (World English Bible)
excerpt: Let his days be few. Let another take his office.
